post-fd-periodic-newtonian.physical_scope: Adopted three-dimensional, incompressible, constant-density and constant-viscosity Newtonian continuum model on a flat periodic cell, with zero body force and no temperature field. Its weak realization uses the unforced periodic Leray–Hopf class. It asserts no empirical universality, global smoothness, or uniqueness.

post-fd-periodic-newtonian:
## Postulate

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval measured in seconds. Fix $L>0$ as the numerical period in the declared SI metre unit, so the physical side length is $L\,\mathrm m$, and use the flat periodic cell $\mathbb T_L^3=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$ with normalized spatial measure $L^{-3}dx$. Spatial coordinates in physical volume integrals are measured in metres. Assume Countable Choice for the stated Fourier and Sobolev space conventions. The velocity is a vector field $u:I\times\mathbb T_L^3\to\mathbb R^3$ with SI units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the mass density is a constant primitive parameter $\rho_0>0$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$; the dynamic viscosity is a constant primitive parameter $\mu>0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$; and the mechanical pressure $p$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$. The body-force density is zero (its SI unit is $\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$), and there is no temperature variable in this model.

For classical fields take $u\in C^1(I;C^2(\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb R^3))$ and $p\in C^1(I;C^1(\mathbb T_L^3))$. Adopt incompressibility $\operatorname{div}u=0$ and the local momentum balance
$$\rho_0\bigl(\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)\bigr)=\operatorname{div}\sigma,\qquad \sigma=-pI_3+2\mu D(u),\qquad D(u)=\tfrac12\bigl(\nabla u+(\nabla u)^{\mathsf T}\bigr).$$
Here $\sigma$ is the Cauchy stress, so its traction on an oriented surface with unit normal $n$ is $\sigma n$; $D(u)$ is the symmetric rate-of-deformation tensor; and $\nabla$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$. Every term in the momentum balance has units $\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$. Since $\operatorname{div}u=0$, this equation is equivalently
$$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)+\nabla\pi=\nu\Delta u,\qquad \nu=\mu/\rho_0>0,\qquad \pi=p/\rho_0.$$
where kinematic viscosity $\nu$ and kinematic pressure $\pi$ have units $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$ and $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-2}}$, respectively. All fields are periodic in each spatial coordinate; this is an ideal cell, not a wall-bounded vessel.

For the weak regime, use the global unforced periodic Leray–Hopf class. The spaces are $H$, the real $L^2$ vector fields whose divergence vanishes distributionally on $\mathbb T_L^3$, with unrestricted constant Fourier mode, and $V=H\cap H^1$, where $H^1$ consists of fields and first weak derivatives in $L^2$; use normalized spatial norms. Here $C_w([0,\infty);H)$ means that $t\mapsto (u(t),h)_H$ is continuous for every fixed $h\in H$; the time-dependent $L^p$ spaces are the corresponding Bochner spaces. A weak velocity has $u\in C_w([0,\infty);H)\cap L^\infty(0,\infty;H)\cap L^2_{\rm loc}(0,\infty;V)$, strongly attains $u_0\in H$ as $t\downarrow0$, and satisfies, for every smooth real periodic divergence-free test field $\phi$ compactly supported in time,
$$
\int_0^\infty\!\bigl[(u,\partial_t\phi)+(u\otimes u,\nabla\phi)-\nu(\nabla u,\nabla\phi)\bigr]dt+(u_0,\phi(0))=0.
$$
The tensor pairing is $L^{-3}\int_{[0,L]^3}u_i u_j\partial_j\phi_i\,dx$, and the gradient pairing is $L^{-3}\int_{[0,L]^3}\partial_j u_i\partial_j\phi_i\,dx$. The class also requires
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_0^t\|\nabla u(s)\|_2^2ds\le\|u_0\|_2^2\qquad(t\ge0),
$$
and a full-measure set $S\subset(0,\infty)$ such that
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_s^t\|\nabla u(\tau)\|_2^2d\tau\le\|u(s)\|_2^2\qquad(s\in S\cup\{0\},\ t\ge s).
$$
This weak convention asserts neither uniqueness nor pressure regularity. These equations and the solution class are adopted model assumptions; they are not deductions that every physical fluid obeys them.

pthm-fd-periodic-weak-continuation.physical_scope: Conditional global weak velocity existence for the three-dimensional constant-density, constant-viscosity, unforced incompressible Newtonian model on a flat periodic cell. No pressure regularity, weak uniqueness, global smoothness, temperature evolution, or empirical universality is claimed.

pthm-fd-periodic-weak-continuation:
## Statement

Let $L>0$ be the numerical period in the declared SI metre unit, with physical side length $L\,\mathrm m$; let $\rho_0>0$ be constant in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$ and $\mu>0$ constant in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$. Set $\nu=\mu/\rho_0>0$. On $\mathbb T_L^3$, use normalized Lebesgue measure $L^{-3}dx$, and let $H$ be the real $L^2$ vector fields whose divergence vanishes distributionally, with unrestricted mean mode, and $V=H\cap H^1$, where $H^1$ consists of fields and first weak derivatives in $L^2$. Here $H^s_\sigma$ means the real Fourier-weighted Sobolev space with weights $(1+L^2|\kappa_k|^2)^s$, Fourier divergence condition $k\cdot\widehat u(k)=0$ for $k\ne0$, and unrestricted constant mode. Let $u_0\in H$ be an initial velocity measured in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Assume Countable Choice. Then the adopted unforced periodic model has a global weak velocity $u\in C_w([0,\infty);H)\cap L^\infty(0,\infty;H)\cap L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(0,\infty;V)$, where $C_w$ means continuity of each fixed $H$-pairing and the time-dependent spaces are strongly measurable Bochner spaces, with $u(0)=u_0$ and strong $H$ trace at zero. For every smooth real periodic divergence-free test field $\phi$ compactly supported in time it satisfies
$$
\int_0^\infty\!\bigl[(u,\partial_t\phi)+(u\otimes u,\nabla\phi)-\nu(\nabla u,\nabla\phi)\bigr]dt+(u_0,\phi(0))=0,
$$
where the spatial pairings use the normalized measure and $(u\otimes u):\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}u_i u_j\partial_j\phi_i$. It also satisfies, for every $t\ge0$,
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_0^t\|\nabla u(s)\|_2^2ds\le\|u_0\|_2^2,
$$
and there is a full-measure set $S\subset(0,\infty)$ such that for every $s\in S\cup\{0\}$ and every $t\ge s$,
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_s^t\|\nabla u(\tau)\|_2^2d\tau\le\|u(s)\|_2^2.
$$
In SI units the kinetic energy is $K(t)=\frac{\rho_0}{2}\int_{[0,L]^3}|u(t,x)|^2dx$, and the inequality implies
$$
K(t)+\mu\int_0^t\int_{[0,L]^3}|\nabla u(s,x)|^2dx\,ds\le K(0).
$$
There is also a full-measure set $S\subset(0,\infty)$ such that for every $s\in S\cup\{0\}$ and every $t\ge s$,
$$
K(t)+\mu\int_s^t\int_{[0,L]^3}|\nabla u(\tau,x)|^2dx\,d\tau\le K(s).
$$
This is a conditional model deduction about velocity; it asserts no pressure regularity, weak uniqueness, global smoothness, or empirical validity.

pthm-fd-smooth-consistency.physical_scope: Smooth divergence-free initial data for the three-dimensional constant- density, constant-viscosity, unforced periodic model. Every Leray–Hopf weak continuation agrees with the smooth solution only on its local smooth interval. No global 3D regularity or uniqueness among arbitrary weak solutions is claimed.

pthm-fd-smooth-consistency:
## Statement

Let $L>0$ be the numerical period in the declared SI metre unit, with physical side length $L\,\mathrm m$; let $\rho_0>0$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $\mu>0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, and $\nu=\mu/\rho_0>0$ in $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$. Let $s\ge4$ be an integer and let $u_0\in H^s_\sigma(\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb R^3)\cap C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb R^3)$ be a divergence-free initial velocity in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Here $H^s_\sigma$ consists of real Fourier-weighted fields with dimensionless weights $(1+L^2|\kappa_k|^2)^s$ and $k\cdot\widehat u_0(k)=0$ for $k\ne0$, with the constant Fourier mode unrestricted. Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Then there are $T>0$, a smooth periodic velocity $v\in C^\infty([0,T]\times\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb R^3)$, and a smooth mean-zero kinematic pressure $\pi_v$, with $v(0)=u_0$, such that
$$\partial_tv+\operatorname{div}(v\otimes v)+\nabla\pi_v=\nu\Delta v,\qquad \operatorname{div}v=0.$$
Every global unforced periodic Leray–Hopf weak continuation $u$ of the same model and data satisfies $u(t)=v(t)$ in $H$ for all $t\in[0,T]$. The physical pressure is $p_v=\rho_0\pi_v$ in $\mathrm{Pa}$. The conclusion applies only while this smooth branch exists; it does not assert global smoothness or uniqueness among arbitrary weak solutions.

post-fd-no-slip-newtonian.physical_scope: Adopted constant-density, positive-viscosity, zero-force incompressible Newtonian continuum on a fixed nonempty bounded open three-dimensional vessel. No-slip is the H_0^1 solenoidal-closure condition; no pointwise trace is asserted on an arbitrary open boundary. The weak result concerns velocity only, and makes no universal empirical or thermal claim.

post-fd-no-slip-newtonian:
## Postulate

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval in seconds and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a fixed nonempty bounded open vessel in Cartesian coordinates measured in metres. Assume Countable Choice for the stated Sobolev space conventions. Define $D_\sigma(\Omega)=\{a\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\operatorname{div}a=0\}$, where divergence is the distributional divergence (equal to the classical divergence for these smooth fields), $H$ as its closure in $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, and $V$ as its closure in $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$; here $H_0^1$ is the closure of compactly supported smooth vector fields in the $H^1$ norm, and $H^1$ uses square-integrable fields and first weak derivatives. The adopted no-slip condition means $u(t)\in V$, not a pointwise boundary value. This closure convention does not identify $V$ with every divergence-free member of $H_0^1$ on an arbitrary open set and does not assert a boundary trace theorem.

Take a constant mass density $\rho_0>0$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, a constant dynamic viscosity $\mu>0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, and zero body-force density in $\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$. For classical fields $u\in C^1(I;C^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3))$ and $p\in C^1(I;C^1(\Omega))$, adopt $\operatorname{div}u=0$, the Cauchy stress $\sigma=-pI_3+2\mu D(u)$ with $D(u)=\tfrac12(\nabla u+(\nabla u)^{\mathsf T})$, and the local balance $\rho_0(\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u))=\operatorname{div}\sigma$ in the interior. The velocity has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, pressure and stress have units $\mathrm{Pa}$, spatial derivatives have units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and $\nu=\mu/\rho_0$ has units $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$. No temperature field is included.

For the weak regime, take $u\in C_w([0,\infty);H)\cap L^\infty(0,\infty;H)\cap L^2_{\rm loc}(0,\infty;V)$, with $u(0)=u_0\in H$ and strong $H$ trace at zero; $u_0$ is an initial velocity in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Here $C_w$ means continuity of every fixed $H$-pairing, and each time-dependent Bochner space uses strongly measurable maps with the indicated norm, locally on every finite interval. Interpret this model through the solenoidal variational identity: for every compactly time-supported $C^1$ curve $\phi:[0,\infty)\to V$,
$$
\int_0^\infty\!\bigl[(u,\partial_t\phi)_{L^2}+(u\otimes u,\nabla\phi)_{L^2}-\nu(\nabla u,\nabla\phi)_{L^2}\bigr]dt+(u_0,\phi(0))_{L^2}=0.
$$
Here all spatial pairings use unnormalized Lebesgue measure on $\Omega$, $(u\otimes u):\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}u_i u_j\partial_j\phi_i$, and $\nabla u:\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}\partial_j u_i\partial_j\phi_i$. In this weak formulation pressure is eliminated by the divergence-free tests; no distributional pressure or corner regularity is postulated. On a smoother boundary, a pointwise zero-trace reading would require a separate trace theorem. This is an adopted fixed-vessel model, not a deduction about every real wall.

pthm-fd-bounded-weak-continuation.physical_scope: Conditional global weak velocity for a constant-density, positive- viscosity, zero-force incompressible Newtonian model on any fixed bounded open three-dimensional vessel. No pointwise boundary trace, pressure regularity, uniqueness, smoothness, thermal evolution, or empirical universality is claimed.

pthm-fd-bounded-weak-continuation:
## Statement

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be any nonempty bounded open set in Cartesian coordinates measured in metres. Define $D_\sigma(\Omega)=\{a\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\operatorname{div}a=0\}$, let $H$ be its $L^2(\Omega)$ closure, and let $V$ be its closure in $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, where $H_0^1$ is the $H^1$ closure of compactly supported smooth fields and $H^1$ has the norm formed from the $L^2$ norms of a field and its first weak derivatives. Let $\rho_0>0$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $\mu>0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, $\nu=\mu/\rho_0$, and $u_0\in H$ be an initial velocity in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Then the adopted unforced no-slip model has
$$
u\in C_w([0,\infty);H)\cap L^\infty(0,\infty;H)\cap L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(0,\infty;V),
$$
where $C_w$ means continuity of every fixed $H$-pairing and the time-dependent spaces are Bochner spaces of strongly measurable maps, with $u(0)=u_0$, strong $H$ trace at zero, and, for every compactly time-supported $C^1$ curve $\phi:[0,\infty)\to V$,
$$
\int_0^\infty\!\bigl[(u,\partial_t\phi)_{L^2}+(u\otimes u,\nabla\phi)_{L^2}-\nu(\nabla u,\nabla\phi)_{L^2}\bigr]dt+(u_0,\phi(0))_{L^2}=0.
$$
It satisfies the initial energy inequality
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_0^t\|\nabla u(s)\|_2^2ds\le\|u_0\|_2^2\qquad(t\ge0),
$$
and a full-measure set $S\subset(0,\infty)$ such that for every $s\in S\cup\{0\}$ and $t\ge s$,
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_s^t\|\nabla u(\tau)\|_2^2d\tau\le\|u(s)\|_2^2.
$$
Here spatial norms and pairings use unnormalized Lebesgue measure, $(u\otimes u):\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}u_i u_j\partial_j\phi_i$, and $\nabla u:\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}\partial_j u_i\partial_j\phi_i$. Thus the SI kinetic energy $E(t)=\frac{\rho_0}{2}\int_\Omega|u(t,x)|^2dx$ obeys
$$
E(t)+\mu\int_0^t\int_\Omega|\nabla u(s,x)|^2dx\,ds\le E(0).
$$
The no-slip condition is only the stated $H_0^1$ closure condition; the result supplies no pressure or pointwise wall trace.

pthm-fd-rectangular-weak-pressure.physical_scope: Conditional no-slip weak velocity and normalized distribution pressure on a finite rectangular vessel, with constant density, positive constant viscosity, and zero force. Pressure is only a spacetime distribution; no L2 estimate, corner regularity, or pointwise wall traction is claimed.

pthm-fd-rectangular-weak-pressure:
## Statement

Let $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(a_i,b_i)\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a finite open rectangle in Cartesian coordinates measured in metres, with $a_i<b_i$. Define $D_\sigma(\Omega)=\{a\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\operatorname{div}a=0\}$, $H$ as its closure in $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, and $V$ as its closure in $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, where $H_0^1$ is the $H^1$ closure of compactly supported smooth vector fields and $H^1$ uses square-integrable fields and first weak derivatives. This convention does not identify $V$ with all divergence-free members of $H_0^1$ on an arbitrary open set and makes no pointwise trace assertion. Let $\rho_0>0$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $\mu>0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, $\nu=\mu/\rho_0>0$, and $u_0\in H$ be an initial velocity in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Assume AC and Countable Choice. In addition, assume the following rectangular test-divergence inverse: for $D_0(\Omega)=\{h\in C_c^\infty(\Omega):\int_\Omega h=0\}$, a continuous linear map $R:D_0(\Omega)\to C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ satisfies $\operatorname{div}(Rh)=h$; for each compact input support there is one compact output support, and every output test-function seminorm is bounded by finitely many input seminorms.

Then there are a weak velocity $u\in C_w([0,\infty);H)\cap L^\infty(0,\infty;H)\cap L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(0,\infty;V)$ and a spacetime distribution $\pi$ on $(0,\infty)\times\Omega$. Here $C_w$ means continuity of every fixed $H$-pairing, and the time-dependent spaces use strongly measurable Bochner maps on finite intervals. The velocity has $u(0)=u_0$ and strong $H$ trace at zero, and for every compactly time-supported $C^1$ curve $\phi:[0,\infty)\to V$ it satisfies
$$
\int_0^\infty\!\bigl[(u,\partial_t\phi)_{L^2}+(u\otimes u,\nabla\phi)_{L^2}-\nu(\nabla u,\nabla\phi)_{L^2}\bigr]dt+(u_0,\phi(0))_{L^2}=0.
$$
All spatial pairings use unnormalized Lebesgue measure, with $(u\otimes u):\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}u_i u_j\partial_j\phi_i$ and $\nabla u:\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}\partial_j u_i\partial_j\phi_i$. For every $t\ge0$ it satisfies
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_0^t\|\nabla u(s)\|_2^2ds\le\|u_0\|_2^2,
$$
and there is a full-measure set $S\subset(0,\infty)$ such that for every $s\in S\cup\{0\}$ and every $t\ge s$,
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_s^t\|\nabla u(\tau)\|_2^2d\tau\le\|u(s)\|_2^2.
$$
Fix one scalar test function $\theta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $\int_\Omega\theta=1$. The spacetime distributional equation and this fixed normalization are
$$
\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)+\nabla\pi=\nu\Delta u,
$$
$$
\langle\pi,a(t)\theta(x)\rangle=0
$$
for every compactly supported smooth temporal test $a$. Such a $\theta$ exists because a product of normalized smooth compactly supported interval bumps belongs to $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ and has integral one. The physical pressure $p=\rho_0\pi$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$, is unique under this fixed scaled normalization, and satisfies
$$
\rho_0\partial_tu+\rho_0\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)+\nabla p=\mu\Delta u
$$
as a spacetime distribution. The SI kinetic energy $E(t)=\frac{\rho_0}{2}\int_\Omega|u(t,x)|^2dx$ obeys $E(t)+\mu\int_0^t\int_\Omega|\nabla u(s,x)|^2dx\,ds\le E(0)$. This conditional result asserts no pressure in $L^2$, corner regularity, or pointwise boundary traction.

rem-fd-thermal-coupling.physical_scope: Comparison of the separate periodic isothermal mechanical branch and the rectangular insulated continuum-heat branch. No coupled temperature evolution, viscous-heating source, or total thermomechanical energy balance is asserted.
